summary: El Grande is a tense area-majority game where lords place knights across Spanish regions to seize control at three scoring checkpoints. Much of the tension comes from bidding on power cards for turn order and secretly committing knights to the castillo before big reveals.
praised: tense simultaneous bidding for turn order
criticised: can feel mean and swingy when majorities flip late
King placement by the last player can feel arbitrary

interaction.detail: Players fight directly over the same regions, repositioning knights to break or hold majorities, while secretly loading the castillo for a surprise placement each round. Almost all meaningful state (the board, King position, regions) is shared; only hands of power cards and the castillo are private.

scoring.why: Majority control of each region at three scoring rounds determines who scores big, so the winner is whoever holds the most valuable majorities when the scoring hits.
scoring.how_you_win: You move and reinforce knights to control the most valuable regions right when scoring occurs, repeating this over nine rounds to finish with the highest total.
